b: The company I work for has an annual holiday party that centers on a drawing for numerous prizes for gift cards, cash, lottery tickets, gift baskets, home goods, tool sets, that sort of thing. All employees are invited to bring their families and are given tickets for the drawings. In addition to the physical prizes, there is also a grand prize of cash.

I am deeply bothered that our CEO and other members of high-level management not only get tickets, but they also win—and accept—prizes. Last year, several of them won multiple prizes, while people making minimum wage won nothing. The executive who organized the drawing won five prizes! The drawing is random, and I am sure nothing nefarious is going on, but I think the optics are problematic.

As a director, I don’t claim anything when my ticket numbers are called. I just can’t take a gift card (or anything of value) from people who are struggling to make ends meet, and I object to my fellow members of management not doing the same. Am I overreacting? Is this something egregious enough that would be covered under our whistleblower policy and should be reported to the board chair? Should I just let it go?
